newsitem.title: USA: Fresenius to sell plant, settle FTC charge.
newsitem.headline: Fresenius to sell plant, settle FTC charge.

text.p: Germany's Fresenius AG and its U.S.-based unit Fresenius USA Inc agreed to sell a production plant to settle anti-trust charges that a proposed acquisition would reduce competition, U.S. regulators said. Under a Federal Trade Commission consent agreement, Fresenius will be required to divest its Lewisberry, Pa.-based facility, which makes a product used in treating patients with chronic kidney failure. The FTC charges stemmed from Fresenius' proposed buyout of National Medical Care Inc. FTC voted 4-1 to approve the pact, with Commissioner Roscoe Starek casting a dissenting vote.

In Setember, W.R. Grace & Co completed the deal under which its National Medical Care Inc kidney dialysis unit was merged with with the dialysis business of Fresenius AG. Grace shareholders received 44.8 percent of the newly created company, Fresenius Medical Care AG
Starek's dissenting statement cited insufficient evidence to show the merger is likely to lessen competition substantially.
"When the evidence on entry, expansion and the absence of anti-competitive effects is as clear as in this case, the issuance of a consent order is unwarranted," he said.

The FTC said Fresenius must sell the plant to Di-Chem Inc of Maple Grove, Minn., or another FTC approved acquirer if the Di-Chem deal fell through. In the interim, Fresenius will be required to maintain the marketability, viability and competitiveness of the facility, the FTC said.
